meta.title: CISS — Algorithm origin & lineage registry

home.title: Who first came up with this algorithm?
home.lede: CISS records the original authors and lineage of the algorithms in public code, with evidence. Code is everywhere now, but where an idea came from is still worth recording.
home.heroCaption: The lineage branching out from Quicksort (C. A. R. Hoare, 1961)
home.heroHint: Select a node to open its record.
home.fieldsAside: {n} algorithms, {m} of them discovered independently more than once
home.p1.b: Every derivation carries evidence and a confidence level. Resemblance alone never earns more than “Related”.
home.p2.b: When several people arrived at the same idea independently, we record each of them as an origin and split the credit.
home.p3.h: When we’re wrong, we fix it
home.p3.b: {p}% of current derivations are verified by direct evidence. The rest are marked “Estimated” and open to public review.
home.cta: Found an incorrect attribution? Let us know.

rankings.lede: Credit scores count direct derivations, indirect descendants, and verified implementations. Weakly evidenced relations count for less, and related ones don’t count at all.
scan.meta: Find the algorithms used in a GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket repository or an npm or PyPI package, along with their original authors.
scan.lede: Enter a repository or package address and we’ll find the algorithms used in the code and list their original authors. Supports GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket repositories and npm and PyPI packages, including game-engine code and shaders for Unity, Godot, and Unreal.
scan.busyNote: Fetching the file list and reading the source. This takes 10–40 seconds depending on repository size.
scan.disclaimer: All detections are “Estimated”. Similar-looking code alone is never treated as derivation or plagiarism.
scan.truncated: This repository is large, so only part of the file list was fetched.
scan.none: No traces of recorded algorithms found. Check whether the core code lives in a different repository.
scan.err.bad_input: Unsupported address. Enter a GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket repository URL, owner/repo, npm:package, or pypi:package.
scan.err.not_found: Repository or package not found. Check the address and make sure it’s public.
scan.err.no_repository: This package isn’t linked to a GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket repository, so it can’t be scanned.
scan.err.rate_limited: Too many scan requests right now. Try again in a minute.
scan.err.too_large: This repository is too large to scan.
scan.err.upstream: The repository host isn’t responding. Try again shortly.
scan.err.network: Couldn’t scan because of a network error. Check your connection and try again.
scan.how.api: The code calls a standard or major library that implements the algorithm. For example, Python sorted() is Timsort, and Unity Mathf.PerlinNoise is Perlin noise.
scan.how.dep: A manifest such as package.json, requirements.txt, go.mod, Cargo.toml, or .csproj declares a library that implements the algorithm.
scan.how.decl: A function or class is declared with a name that matches the algorithm’s name.
scan.how.mention: The algorithm’s name is mentioned in code or comments.
scan.how.score: Evidence of the same kind in the same file counts once. The four strongest pieces of evidence are combined with noisy-OR, and only results of 0.5 or higher are reported.

about.meta: How CISS defines an algorithm, derivations, evidence grades, and credit scores.
about.lede: A record that assigns credit has to say up front what it counts and how. Here are all of the definitions and calculations CISS uses.
about.unit.b1: An algorithm is an idea, not a particular piece of code. Procedures that solve the same problem with the same core invariant count as one algorithm, regardless of implementation language or minor optimizations.
about.unit.b2: If the core invariant or complexity bound changes, or the original paper presents it as a separate method, we register a new algorithm and link it with a derivation. This is the v1 working definition for an open question in the PRD, and it will be refined through public review.
about.model.algorithm.d: An abstract idea. Has a name, a definition, a field, and an origin.
about.model.origin.d: The earliest source: a paper DOI, technical report, first commit, or public document, plus the year it appeared. Independent discoveries are recorded as multiple origins.
about.model.author: Author
about.model.author.d: A person or organization named in an origin. Names are written exactly as they appear in public publications.
about.model.implementation.d: Actual code. Recorded by repository, file path, and symbol, with a check that the path really exists.
about.model.derivation.d: A directed relation between algorithms. Always carries a type, evidence, and a confidence level.
about.type.variant: Keeps the core idea but changes part of the procedure.
about.type.optimization: Solves the same problem in less time or space.
about.type.generalization: Extends to a broader problem or input, making the original algorithm a special case.
about.type.composition: Combines existing algorithms as building blocks.
about.type.port: Carries the same structure over to a different mathematical object or environment.
about.evidence.b: Line style shows the strength of evidence. Similar code alone is never called a derivation.
about.score.b: The credit score counts how much has followed from an idea. Weaker evidence and more distant generations count for less.
about.score.example: Example: an algorithm with {d} direct derivations, {n} descendants, and {i} implementations scores {s}.
about.score.note: These weights are a first version for open questions in the PRD (indirect derivation weight, time decay). Any change will be reflected on this page and in the dataset’s score field.
about.sources.b1: The Phase 0 seed DB covers {a} textbook algorithms, curated by hand from original papers and standard references. Of these, {o} were discovered independently more than once and are recorded with multiple origins.
about.sources.b2: Of {n} paper DOIs and arXiv IDs, {c} were checked against Crossref, OpenAlex, and arXiv metadata to confirm that titles and years match.
about.sources.b3: For {i} notable implementations, we confirmed that the file and symbol actually exist on each repository’s default branch.
about.p0.b: Hand-curated classic algorithms, lineage graph, source cross-checks.
about.p1.b: Algorithm pages, lineage graph, search, contributor profiles, 4 languages.
about.p2.b: Repo scans for GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, npm, and PyPI. This is a rule-based v1; code embeddings and LLM classification come next.
about.p3.b: Claims and disputes with public review, rankings by field, README badges.
about.p4.h: Phase 4 data assets — public API live
about.p4.b: REST API, OpenAPI spec, JSON and CSV dataset dumps.
about.privacy.b: Contributor names come only from public publications and public repositories. We don’t collect commit emails, and contact details from disputes are seen only by reviewers and never exposed through the public API. We make a profile private at its owner’s request.
about.disclaimer: CISS records origins. It does not rule on plagiarism, license violations, or legal disputes.
dev.meta: CISS public API, OpenAPI spec, dataset dumps, and README badges.
dev.lede: All lineage data is available as-is through the public API and datasets. The read API requires no authentication and allows CORS.
dev.ep.algorithms: List algorithms with credit metrics. Use field to filter by field.
dev.ep.algorithm: Algorithm details: origins, parent and child edges, implementations, lineage.
dev.ep.author: Contributor details and per-field scores.
dev.ep.search: Search algorithms and contributors. Use locale to set the language of supplementary text.
dev.ep.dataset: Full dataset as a JSON dump (schema ciss-lineage/1).
dev.ep.csv: Per-table CSV: algorithms, origins, derivations, authors, implementations.
dev.ep.scan: Repository or package scan report. Cached for 6 hours.
dev.ep.claims: Public claims and disputes. Contact details are not included.
dev.ep.claimPost: Submit a claim or dispute. Requires 1–5 evidence links.
dev.ep.badge: SVG badge for READMEs. Also supports the author kind.
dev.badgesBody: Copy the Markdown from any algorithm or contributor page and paste it into your README to credit the original authors of the algorithms you use, right on your repository’s front page.
dev.policy.cors: The read API can be called from any origin (CORS *).
dev.policy.rate: Repo scans are limited to about 3 per minute per IP, and request submissions to about 2 per minute.
dev.policy.privacy: Contact details from disputes are stored but never exposed through any API.
dev.policy.env: When self-hosting, raise host request limits with GITHUB_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN, and BITBUCKET_TOKEN, and enable review with CISS_ADMIN_TOKEN.
